speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is concerning for an intestinal obstruction. To start our evaluation, can you tell me exactly how many days old the baby is and when these symptoms first began?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand you are a newborn presenting with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. While the history of pyloric stenosis in your brother is noted, the presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn born at term strongly suggests a distal intestinal obstruction rather than gastroenteritis, which is typically associated with diarrhea and fever. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out critical conditions like malrotation with volvulus, I must examine your abdomen and review the imaging I have requested. Please allow me to proceed with the physical exam and review the X-ray results to ensure your safety.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Volvulus
